summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from RIT with embedded firmware experience across STM32 (bare-metal C), NVIDIA Jetson (embedded Linux), and FreeRTOS. Deployed real-hardware systems integrating UART/I2C/SPI/ToF sensors with interrupt-driven real-time control; experienced with oscilloscopes and PCB design.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python over UART.
Implemented a custom z-axis differential tap-detection algorithm; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and ADC resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotion robots; implemented closed-loop sensor communication over UART and I2C.
Led 25-member team across national robotics competitions owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end-to-end.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: TensorRT-optimized YOLO for real-time visual servoing (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS); dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.
Embedded Linux deployment on NVIDIA Jetson: production systemd service with SIGTERM handling, WebSocket auto-reconnect, and serial UART passthrough to Arduino C++ controller.
Resolved 11 integration failures; 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: STM32 firmware (bare-metal C / FreeRTOS): interrupt-driven UART command parser, multi-servo PWM control, mutex-protected shared state, and VL53L0X ToF over I2C with OLED display.
Validated PWM timing and signal integrity with oscilloscope; tuned dead-band limits under real servo load with YOLO-on-Jetson sending real-time UART commands.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Cortex-M4 firmware in C: timer-triggered ADC scan, interrupt-driven sample capture, low-level I2C driver — direct register access (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1).
3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz; verified timing in Proteus simulation.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Delivery Drone
bullets: Arduino C++ flight controller: clamped PWM to 4× SimonK ESCs, Bluetooth command parser, ESC arming; Jetson systemd service with SIGTERM handling and serial UART passthrough (Restart=always).

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
